title: The Order That Never Enrolled Anyone: Proclamations, the Frankish Koran, and a Long Wandering to the Ticino
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Judge's Circuit in Lower Franconia

stops.name: Gerolzhofen, the judge's son
stops.date_confidence: Attested. Birth on 3 November 1870 at Gerolzhofen per Deutsche Biographie (gnd11852478X), Literaturportal Bayern, and both Wikipedias. Coordinate corrected to Ludwig-Derleth-Strasse, Gerolzhofen (49.9013, 10.3505, OSM/Nominatim); a commonly circulated pin at 49.9081, 10.3486 misses the street by roughly 770 m to the north.
stops.campa: A son is born to Johann Derleth, Bavarian district judge, and to his wife Maria, born Strobel, in the wine town of Gerolzhofen in Lower Franconia. They name him Ludwig Benjamin. The house stands on a street the town will one day rename for him. Franconia is what he gets and what he never afterwards puts down: the Catholic liturgical year, the Latin of the courtroom and the Latin of the mass, vineyard country still lying under the memory of its prince-bishops. In 1932 he will publish that province under the title of a world scripture.
suggested_refs: The birth house on what is now Ludwig-Derleth-Strasse, Gerolzhofen

stops.name: Stadtprozelten, the first of the postings
stops.date_confidence: Residence attested, date not. The Lower Franconian moves follow the father's judicial appointments and no reachable source dates any of them; 1875 is an ordering device only. Coordinate corrected from 49.7639, 9.3878, which fell about 2.3 km outside the town in the Main valley woods; Stadtprozelten geocodes to 49.7809, 9.4053 (OSM/Nominatim).
stops.campa: The judge is posted and the household moves with him. Stadtprozelten is a market town on a bend of the Main, castle above, vines on the slope, a few hundred souls below. Here the boy begins the practice he will never afterwards call a discipline. He is the new family in a small Catholic town, watched at mass and in the street, holding to a rule of his own inside a place that already has its rule and has no use for his. Not one day of it is recorded.
suggested_refs: Bavarian judicial-service records for Johann Derleth's Lower Franconian postings

stops.name: Bischofsheim in der Rhoen, the second posting
stops.date_confidence: Residence attested, date not; 1880 orders the segment and rests on nothing. Coordinate corrected from 50.3958, 10.0119, off by about 1.5 km mostly in longitude; Bischofsheim in der Rhoen geocodes to 50.4012, 9.9934 (OSM/Nominatim).
stops.campa: Higher country now: the basalt domes of the Rhoen, forest and thin pasture, pilgrimage chapels standing on the ridges where the wind gets at them. The Derleths move again, and again the record keeps only a place-name. The father administers the law of the Kingdom of Bavaria. The mother breaks the house up and remakes it at every transfer. The boy arrives a stranger in each town and is moved on before he has stopped being one. What the childhood contained, as against what shape it had, nobody wrote down.
suggested_refs: The Rhoen pilgrimage chapels of the Bischofsheim district

stops.name: Muennerstadt, the Gymnasium
stops.date_confidence: Schooling at Muennerstadt attested (Literaturportal Bayern; das-blaettchen.de); the year is not, and 1884 orders the segment. Coordinate corrected: 50.2497, 10.1917 sits about 2.2 km southwest of the town, and the Johann-Philipp-von-Schoenborn-Gymnasium geocodes to 50.2526, 10.1875 (OSM/Nominatim). FLAGGED: the claim that he later returned to Muennerstadt as a teacher of ancient languages appears in English Wikipedia only and is absent from Literaturportal Bayern, which is usually cited for it.
stops.campa: The Gymnasium at Muennerstadt takes him for the Latin and Greek years. Here the ancient languages stop being a subject and become the medium he thinks in. He is drilled in the accusative absolute and in the imperative mood, and it is the imperative that stays with him: every important sentence he writes as an adult is an order issued to somebody, in a language dead long enough to make orders sound like liturgy. Some accounts have the town keeping him again, decades later, on the other side of the lectern.
suggested_refs: The Johann-Philipp-von-Schoenborn-Gymnasium, Muennerstadt

stops.name: Nuremberg, the last of the postings
stops.date_confidence: Residence attested, everything else [R]. Literaturportal Bayern names Nuremberg among the childhood towns and gives neither an Abitur nor a year; the widely repeated school-leaving of 1889 is carried by no source reached and is marked reconstruction. 1888 is an ordering date. Coordinate is central Nuremberg, about 0.8 km from the city centroid.
stops.campa: The last of the father's postings brings the family to Nuremberg, the largest place the boy has lived: a Protestant free city with a Catholic minority, and a medieval skyline that has been an argument about German identity since Duerer painted himself as Christ in it. Whether he takes his school-leaving certificate here, and in which year, is stated by no reachable source; the figure 1889 circulates without a document beneath it. He goes on to Munich with his Greek and his Latin, at some point in these years.
suggested_refs: Nuremberg Gymnasium records for the late 1880s, not located

segments.name: Munich: Philology, Psychiatry, and the Dismissal

stops.name: Munich, the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitaet
stops.date_confidence: Attested that he studied at Munich (Deutsche Biographie; Literaturportal Bayern). CONTRADICTION FLAGGED, not resolved: the subject list differs, Deutsche Biographie and Literaturportal Bayern giving classical philology, philosophy and psychiatry, English Wikipedia adding German literature and the natural sciences. No completed doctorate, dissertation or supervisor is documented anywhere. 1891 is an ordering date; no enrolment year is stated in reachable sources.
stops.campa: He matriculates at Munich and reads classical philology, philosophy, and psychiatry, a combination that will look like prophecy to his admirers and like a diagnosis to everyone else. He finishes no doctorate. What the years produce instead is a private syllabus assembled against the official one: the Church Fathers, the Roman imperial idea, and Nietzsche, whose Zarathustra hands him the single thing a philology seminar cannot, a form for speaking as though from above and being obeyed.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitaet, not consulted

stops.name: Dillingen an der Donau, twelve years of ancient languages
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the Dillingen posting. The roughly twelve years of Bavarian Gymnasium teaching are attested (en.wikipedia); Dillingen rests on a bibliographic citation only, Hans Boehm in Jahrbuch des Historischen Vereins Dillingen 67/68 (1965/66), which is not online and was not retrieved. Literaturportal Bayern names no teaching towns at all. 1894 is an ordering date. Coordinate corrected from 48.5717, 10.4838, about 1 km off; Dillingen an der Donau geocodes to 48.5772, 10.4944 (OSM/Nominatim).
stops.campa: For twelve years or thereabouts he stands in front of Bavarian schoolboys and takes them through Homer and Cicero. Dillingen on the Danube, an old prince-bishops' university town demoted to a Gymnasium seat, is where a local archivist placed part of that stretch in a study nobody since has managed to open. It is the least visible period of the life and the most productive: a salaried servant of the Kingdom of Bavaria, correcting exercises by day and writing at night the sentences that will get him taken for a lunatic.
suggested_refs: Hans Boehm, Jahrbuch des Historischen Vereins Dillingen 67/68 (1965/66), on the Dillingen Gymnasialarchiv
sources: Hans Boehm, Jahrbuch des Historischen Vereins Dillingen 67/68 (1965/66), cited but not retrieved

stops.name: Munich-Schwabing, Kessler and the journal Pan
stops.date_confidence: The publication is attested in the standard Derleth bibliography: 'Anadyomene' in Pan, vol. 3, November 1896, over the byline 'Ludwig B. Derleth'. [R] for Harry Graf Kessler's role in placing it, which comes through Deutsche Biographie and Literaturportal Bayern as summarized in the dossier rather than from a document examined here. Stop pinned to Schwabing, where Derleth was; Pan was produced in Berlin.
stops.campa: Harry Graf Kessler, who collects new writers the way other men collect prints, notices him in the Schwabing literary world and passes his name to Pan in Berlin. In the third volume, that November, a piece called Anadyomene appears over the byline Ludwig B. Derleth. It is the first time his name is set in type by anyone other than a school. He is twenty-six, a salaried teacher of Latin in the Bavarian provinces, printed in the most expensively produced arts journal in the German language.
suggested_refs: Pan, vol. 3 (Berlin, 1896), containing 'Anadyomene'

stops.name: Munich, Dimissus ob defectum vocationis
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The Latin note and its date of 6 October 1897 are reported tradition transmitted through Dominik Jost's biography; neither the document nor the institution has been independently examined, and no accessible secondary literature identifies the house of formation. Pinned to Munich, his place of residence, precisely because the institution is unnamed.
stops.campa: An archival note in Latin, dated the sixth of October, records that he is dismissed from a religious formation for lack of vocation. Four words settle it. The institution is named in nothing that can be read today, and the tradition survives only through his biographer. What follows is not obscure at all: a man refused the priesthood spends the next fifty years founding an order of his own, drafting its rule, drilling its imaginary novices, and recruiting for it in rented rooms.
stops.quote_source: Latin archival note dated 6 October 1897, reported via Dominik Jost's biography of Derleth
suggested_refs: Dominik Jost, Ludwig Derleth: Gestalt und Leistung (Stuttgart, 1965)
sources: Tradition reported via Dominik Jost's biography, not independently examined

stops.name: Paris, the year of Kolbe
stops.date_confidence: Attested for the stay and the meeting: the Georg Kolbe Museum object record states 'Georg Kolbe lernte den charismatischen Dichter und schwaermerischen Sektierer 1898 in Paris kennen'. CORRECTIONS: the same record calls the tie to Derleth's sister a love relationship, not an engagement, does not name her, and gives no end date, saying only that Kolbe broke it off after leaving Paris. CONTRADICTION FLAGGED on Stefan George: the Paris route is one tradition, while de.wikisource's editorial note to the poem 'An Derleth' has George knowing him through the circle of the Munich Kosmiker; not resolved. The often-repeated claim that Derleth recruited young men in Paris for a projected religious-military order is [R] and is carried by no source reached. Coordinate is central Paris, city level only; no address is established.
stops.campa: He makes an extended stay in Paris, and in Paris he meets the young sculptor Georg Kolbe. Kolbe will one day cut his head in stone; first he falls in love with Derleth's sister and breaks it off when he leaves the city. The museum record calls Derleth what nearly everyone who met him called him, a charismatic poet and a rapturous sectarian. How Stefan George comes into the story is disputed. One tradition runs through this Paris year, another through the Munich cosmics, and the two sources do not agree.
stops.quote_source: Derleth's stated early motto, quoted in J. Aler, 'Ludwig Derleth (1870-1948)', in Gestalten um St. George (Amsterdam, 1985), p. 115, as reproduced in Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona'
suggested_refs: Georg Kolbe Museum, object record 'Portraet Ludwig Derleth' (sammlung.georg-kolbe-museum.de, object 62955)
sources: de.wikisource, editorial note to Stefan George, 'An Derleth'

stops.name: Munich-Schwabing, among the Kosmiker
stops.date_confidence: Attested that Derleth associated with the Munich Kosmiker around Alfred Schuler and Ludwig Klages, and that the circle broke up in 1904 (en.wikipedia; de.wikipedia, 'Kosmiker'). 1901 is an ordering date; the year he entered the circle is not fixed by any source reached.
stops.campa: In Schwabing he moves in the circle around Alfred Schuler and Ludwig Klages, men who call themselves cosmics and hold that the modern world can be cured by pagan Rome, by blood, by the swastika read as a solar sign decades before anyone marches beneath it. Derleth sits among them with a rival answer already drafted. He wants antiquity back as well, but the antiquity that converted: emperor and Church together, legion under rule, the Caesar who kneels. For a season the disagreement fits in one room.
suggested_refs: de.wikipedia, 'Kosmiker', on the Schwabing circle and its 1904 dissolution

stops.name: Munich, the break with Schuler
stops.date_confidence: Attested for the dating: Literaturportal Bayern has the friendship with Schuler ended by 1902, and de.wikipedia 'Kosmiker' supports the substance, naming the competing renewals as Roman antiquity for Schuler and early Christianity for Derleth. CORRECTION: the 'emperor and Galilean' formulation is Dominik Jost's and is attributed to him directly; it appears in neither Deutsche Biographie nor Literaturportal Bayern as fetched.
stops.campa: The friendship with Schuler ends. What divides them is exactly what had looked like agreement. Both want antiquity restored, but Schuler wants the matriarchal pagan Rome that Christianity killed, and Derleth wants early Christianity armed, hierarchical, and imperial. His biographer will frame the split as the frontier between the emperor and the Galilean. The circle itself outlasts the quarrel by two years and then dissolves, and its survivors spend the rest of their lives arguing about what it had been.
stops.quote: Das Aufwerfen kosmischer Damme gegen den Wahnsinn der Vernunft ist kein Werk logischer Tatigkeit.
stops.quote_source: Ludwig Derleth, Das Werk, quoted at journals.openedition.org/germanica/3693, which renders it 'Erecting cosmic dams against the madness of reason is not a work of logical activity'. German transcribed as fetched, with umlauts stripped in the source consulted.
suggested_refs: Dominik Jost's account of the Schuler split, in Ludwig Derleth: Gestalt und Leistung (1965)

stops.name: Munich, Kolbe cuts the head
stops.date_confidence: Attested that Georg Kolbe made a portrait bust of Derleth, dated 1904 in English Wikipedia and held in the Georg Kolbe Museum's collection record. Contributions to Stefan George's Blaetter fuer die Kunst are attested across roughly 1896 to 1910; the 1902 date sometimes given for the first of them is an approximation and no individual issue was examined here.
stops.campa: Georg Kolbe, six years on from Paris, makes a portrait bust of him. The face that comes out of the clay is the one the anecdotes describe: narrow, ascetic, the eyes fixed on somebody who is not in the room. In these same years his poems and prose appear in Stefan George's Blaetter fuer die Kunst, the most closed and most fastidious publication in Germany, which prints nothing it has not first approved of morally. He is thirty-four, and his readers are counted in the hundreds.
suggested_refs: Georg Kolbe's portrait bust of Ludwig Derleth, Georg Kolbe Museum
Blaetter fuer die Kunst, the George-circle series

stops.name: Munich, Destouchesstrasse, the reading in Good Friday week
stops.date_confidence: Attested: three evening readings of the still-unpublished Proklamationen, with Thomas Mann present at one of the three (de.wikipedia, 'Kosmiker'), the invitation falling 'in der Karfreitagswoche 1904', Good Friday week (de.wikipedia, 'Beim Propheten'; das-blaettchen gives Easter week). [R] for the precise day: Good Friday 1904 did fall on 1 April, so the usual arithmetic is sound, but the day itself is a reconstruction. The address Destouchesstrasse 1 is UNCONFIRMED, the stadtgeschichte-muenchen.de address-book page cited for it returning 404; the coordinate is Destouchesstrasse 1 per OSM/Nominatim, correcting a circulated 48.1595 that sits about 580 m south. Franziska zu Reventlow's presence and a next-day letter to Kurt Martens are [R], attested in nothing reachable. Thomas Mann has no journey file in this atlas.
stops.campa: Over three evenings in his own rooms a disciple reads the still unpublished Proklamationen aloud to invited guests. It is a rule, a call to arms, and a liturgy at once, addressed to an order that does not exist, spoken in the voice of a Christ who commands legions. Thomas Mann is at one of the three. He goes home and writes 'Beim Propheten', a story about a starving fanatic in an attic dictating the conquest of the world, and forty-three years later raises the same figure again as Daniel zur Hoehe in Doktor Faustus.
stops.quote: We subdue the world or it perishes.
stops.quote_source: Ludwig Derleth, Proklamationen (1904), quoted in Hans Urs von Balthasar, 'Integralismus' (1963), trans. Charles Hughes Huff and Anne Carpenter, theologyandsociety.com
suggested_refs: Thomas Mann, 'Beim Propheten' (1904)
Thomas Mann, Doktor Faustus (1947), ch. XXXIV, the figure of Daniel zur Hoehe

stops.name: Leipzig, Insel Verlag prints the Proclamations
stops.date_confidence: Attested for publisher, place, year and extent: K10plus gives Leipzig, Insel-Verlag, 1904, 83 Seiten. [R] for the precise date of 1 December 1904 and for the frequently repeated '500 numbered copies on handmade paper', neither of which appears in the catalogue record or in Literaturportal Bayern as fetched; 1904-12-01 is used here to order the segment. Publication-site stop: Derleth's own presence in Leipzig is not established. The quoted lines are recorded, not endorsed.
stops.campa: Insel Verlag issues Die Proklamationen at Leipzig, eighty-three pages. In them a voice that is neither quite Christ's nor quite Derleth's summons an elite, declares war on the modern world, and seals the age. The book also prints plain antisemitism as command. It sells almost nothing, and it is read by nearly everyone who counts in German letters. The reputation for madness dates from this book, and he carries it for the remaining forty-four years of his life.
stops.quote: War and Cross. Shoot the ecumenical synagogue on fire.
stops.quote_source: Ludwig Derleth, Proklamationen (1904), quoted in Hans Urs von Balthasar, 'Integralismus' (1963), trans. Charles Hughes Huff and Anne Carpenter, theologyandsociety.com. Two adjacent lines within the block quotation Balthasar reproduces. Antisemitic content stated as recorded, not endorsed.
suggested_refs: Die Proklamationen (Leipzig: Insel-Verlag, 1904), 83 pp.
Hans Urs von Balthasar, 'Integralismus' (1963), which quotes the Proklamationen at length
sources: K10plus catalogue record for Die Proklamationen, Leipzig 1904

stops.name: Munich, out of the school service
stops.date_confidence: Attested that he left Bavarian Gymnasium service in 1906 and became an independent writer (Literaturportal Bayern; consistent with English Wikipedia's freelance-writer framing). No dismissal, disciplinary record, or pension dispute is documented in any source consulted; the record says only that he left the school service.
stops.campa: He leaves Bavarian Gymnasium service and becomes a freelance writer. No dismissal, no disciplinary file, no pension dispute appears anywhere in the record. A teacher of ancient languages simply stops teaching at thirty-five and never takes another salaried post in the forty-two years remaining to him. From here the money is intermittent and largely other people's, and his sister keeps the household. The Proklamationen have by now been in print long enough for the anecdotes to have overtaken the book.
stops.quote_source: Ludwig Derleth, Proklamationen (1904), quoted in Hans Urs von Balthasar, 'Integralismus' (1963), trans. Charles Hughes Huff and Anne Carpenter, theologyandsociety.com
suggested_refs: Bavarian school-service personnel files for Derleth, not located

stops.name: Lugano, an essay for a secular cenobium
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The essay 'Per un cenobio laico' in the Lugano journal Coenobium is reported in secondary Derleth scholarship (Georg Doerr) and was not independently located or read. Publication-site stop, pinned to Lugano where Coenobium was produced; Derleth's own presence in Lugano is not established.
stops.campa: In the Lugano journal Coenobium he publishes an argument in Italian for a secular cenobium, a communal religious life led by men who are not priests. It is the Proklamationen with the shouting taken out and the architecture left standing: a rule, a house, a common table, vows and hours and obedience. He is proposing in print, in a foreign language, at thirty-seven, exactly what a Latin note refused him in private ten years before. Nobody founds it. Nobody ever founds it.
suggested_refs: Ludwig Derleth, 'Per un cenobio laico', Coenobium (Lugano, 1907), not located
sources: Reported via Georg Doerr's Derleth scholarship, not independently located

stops.name: Munich, George addresses him a poem
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Stefan George's poem 'An Derleth' stands in the 'Tafeln' section of Der siebente Ring (1907), and Derleth's contributions to the Blaetter fuer die Kunst run to about 1910, after which close contact with George's circle ends (en.wikipedia; Deutsche Biographie; Literaturportal Bayern). No quarrel or breaking point is recorded by any source reached. Pinned to Munich, where Derleth was living.
stops.campa: Stefan George prints 'An Derleth' among the Tafeln of Der siebente Ring, the tablets in which he assigns each man near him a fixed place in a hierarchy he alone administers. To be given a Tafel is to be recognized and at the same instant filed. Derleth goes on sending work to the Blaetter fuer die Kunst until about 1910, and then the close contact ends. No quarrel is on record, no letter of rupture, nothing but the contributions stopping. Der siebente Ring is published at Berlin in 1907.
suggested_refs: Stefan George, 'An Derleth', in the 'Tafeln' of Der siebente Ring (1907)

segments.name: The Mediterranean and the Near East

stops.name: Algiers, the African crossing
stops.date_confidence: [R] for everything but the bare fact of a journey. Literaturportal Bayern lists 'Algerien' among his travels with no itinerary, no ports and no dates; en.wikipedia gives the same undifferentiated list. 1908 is an ordering device with no documentary basis whatever. Coordinate is central Algiers, chosen as the country's principal arrival point, and is not a confirmed stop.
stops.campa: The biographies list Algeria among his travels and then say nothing further. He crosses to Africa, at some point, for some length of time, in a decade that leaves behind no letters and no notebook. What comes back with him is not an itinerary but a vocabulary: desert, minaret, recitation, the muezzin's long cadence that he will graft onto Franconian Catholicism and publish under a title designed to affront both parties to the graft. The whole documentary basis for this stop is one word in a list.
suggested_refs: Literaturportal Bayern's undated list of Derleth's Mediterranean and Near Eastern travels

stops.name: Carthage, the burnt city under the grid
stops.date_confidence: [R]. Carthage is named among Derleth's Mediterranean travels in Literaturportal Bayern with no date and no indication of which sites he saw; June 1908 is an ordering device. Budapest and Syria stand in the same undated list and are not given separate pins in this file, being unlocatable to any site.
stops.campa: Carthage is named among his journeys. He stands, if the list is true, on the Byrsa hill where Rome destroyed a civilization and then built its own colony on top of the ash. Punic cisterns, Roman baths, a French basilica of Saint Louis on the summit. His own program is the Roman imperial idea baptized and rearmed, and here the idea stands with its price attached: a killed city under a Roman street grid under a French protectorate. No letter, no notebook and no date survives from the visit.
suggested_refs: The Byrsa hill excavations at Carthage under the French protectorate

stops.name: Rhodes, the knights' walled town
stops.date_confidence: [R]. Rhodes appears in the same undated travel list (Literaturportal Bayern); no site on the island is documented and 1909 is an ordering date only. The island was Ottoman until 1912 and Italian afterwards, so even the sovereignty he would have found there cannot be determined.
stops.campa: Rhodes appears in the list. The old town is a walled crusader city raised by the Knights Hospitaller, a military religious order that held territory, garrisoned it, drew revenue, and answered to a grand master under a written rule. Chapels, auberges by nation, a hospital, a palace, all inside one circuit of wall. That is, item for item, the institution Derleth spends his life trying to reconstitute for the twentieth century. Whether he sees the correspondence, or whether the island is simply where a boat calls, no source says.
suggested_refs: The Hospitaller fortifications of Rhodes old town

stops.name: Baalbek, the six standing columns
stops.date_confidence: [R], and the pin is a mapping reconstruction rather than an itinerary point. Literaturportal Bayern names only 'Libanon' among his travels, with no city and no date; Baalbek is used here as the region's most prominent landmark and is not a confirmed stop. 1910 orders the segment.
stops.campa: Lebanon is on the list; no city is. Baalbek stands in for it here, the largest Roman temple complex ever built, six columns of the Temple of Jupiter still upright above the Bekaa with an Arab town at their feet. The stones are cut to a scale that argues for empire in the only language empire has ever spoken well. Place by undocumented place, he is assembling the geography that will later be recited, in Franconian German, out of a book he insists on calling a Koran.
suggested_refs: The Temple of Jupiter at Baalbek, used here as a regional landmark, not an attested stop

stops.name: Babylon, the excavated field
stops.date_confidence: [R], pin reconstructed for mapping. The travel lists name only 'Irak'; no city or site is specified in any source reached, and the ruins of Babylon are used as the region's most prominent landmark. June 1910 orders the segment and rests on nothing. Robert Koldewey's German excavation at Babylon, running from 1899, is attested independently but no source connects Derleth to it.
stops.campa: Iraq closes the list. Babylon in these years is a low brown field of German trenches: Robert Koldewey has been digging since 1899 and is shipping the Ishtar Gate to Berlin in crates. Whether Derleth goes anywhere near it cannot be established. What can be said is that the Near East enters his writing as scripture and never as travel, the place-names handled the way a liturgy handles them, and that nothing in his published work reads like a man describing something he saw.
suggested_refs: Robert Koldewey's Deutsche Orient-Gesellschaft excavations at Babylon, 1899-1917

stops.name: Munich, the convert and the wife to be
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Regina Ullmann converted to Catholicism in 1911, 'apparently under Ludwig Derleth's influence' (en.wikipedia, 'Regina Ullmann'), and Derleth met Christine Ulrich in 1911 (en.wikipedia, 'Ludwig Derleth'). [R] for the spiritual exercises at Altoetting and the month of November, in no source reached. Derleth's own presence at Altoetting is not established, so this stop is pinned to Munich, where he was, rather than staged at the shrine, which is Ullmann's stop and not his. Regina Ullmann has no journey file in this atlas. Christine Ulrich's parentage, Christian Ulrich and Maria Baartz of Darmstadt, is [R] from the Wikipedia articles.
stops.campa: The writer Regina Ullmann, of a Jewish family and in personal distress, turns Catholic this year, apparently under Derleth's influence. The tradition adds spiritual exercises at Altoetting that November, though nothing places him there beside her. In the same year he meets Christine Ulrich, born at Darmstadt in 1894, sister of his friend Wilhelm Ulrich. He is forty-one; she is seventeen. They will marry in Rome thirteen years later, when he is fifty-three and she is twenty-nine.
suggested_refs: Regina Ullmann's 1911 conversion, in the standard Ullmann biographical accounts

stops.name: Munich, Marienplatz, the brother and the sister
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Anna Maria Derleth (1874-1955) and the lifelong shared household (en.wikipedia; Lothar Helbing, 'Ludwig und Anna Maria Derleth. Eine Sammlung von Berichten', in the Ludwig-Derleth-Gedenkbuch, Amsterdam 1958, pp. 5-128). [R] for the address: the Kalliope authority record for GND 11852478X lists only Gerolzhofen, Munich and San Pietro di Stabio as Wirkungsorte and carries no street addresses; the house number 2 is unsupported, and the Marienplatz association survives only through Christine Derleth's memoir as quoted by Georg Doerr, where Olga Froebe sits 'am Marienplatz Ludwig gegenueber'. The middle name 'Regina' sometimes given to the sister is likewise unsupported. Coordinate is Marienplatz 2 per OSM/Nominatim. 1916 is an ordering date; the years of residence are unknown.
stops.campa: He keeps house with his sister Anna Maria, born in 1874, who will outlive him by seven years and whose entire recorded conversation is her brother. Viktor Mann remembers the arrangement from the far side of Munich society: he cannot swear Ludwig ever came to them, but when the sister accepted his mother's invitation the brother was at least spiritually present, since in company she spoke of hardly anything else. Olga Froebe-Kapteyn will later sit across a table from him at the Marienplatz.
stops.quote: Ich weiss nicht mehr bestimmt, ob Ludwig Derleth je selbst zu uns gekommen ist. Aber wenn seine Schwester Mamas Einladung folgte, dann war der Bruder zum mindesten geistig auch zugegen, denn sie sprach in Gesellschaft kaum etwas anderes als von ihm.
stops.quote_source: Viktor Mann, Wir waren funf (1949), quoted at journals.openedition.org/germanica/3693
suggested_refs: Lothar Helbing, 'Ludwig und Anna Maria Derleth', in the Ludwig-Derleth-Gedenkbuch (Amsterdam, 1958)
sources: Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona' (georgdoerr.net)

stops.name: Munich, the Musarion edition
stops.date_confidence: Attested. K10plus: 'Proklamationen', Ludwig Derleth, edition statement '1.-4. Tsd.', Muenchen, Musarion-Verlag, 1919, 132 S.; de.wikipedia 'Kosmiker' calls it 'eine leicht abgeaenderte Version'. CORRECTION: accounts giving the place vaguely as 'Germany' and omitting the publisher are corrected here to Munich and Musarion. That the moderation is a response to the political temperature is inference, not a sourced claim.
stops.campa: Fifteen years and a world war after the first printing, the Proklamationen appear again from Musarion in Munich, a hundred and thirty-two pages, first through fourth thousand, in a slightly altered version. What has altered is the temperature. A book that in 1904 read as one man's private lunacy now lands in a Munich of Freikorps columns and a soviet republic put down by machine gun, and reads there as a program. He tones it down. It is the first sign in the record that he can hear how he sounds.
suggested_refs: Proklamationen, Munich: Musarion-Verlag, 1919, 132 pp., first through fourth thousand

stops.name: Munich, the first letter from The Hague
stops.date_confidence: Attested that the surviving correspondence opens with a sheet headed 'Haag, 27. Aug. 20' and runs until Derleth's death (Georg Doerr, from the Derleth-Nachlass at the Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach). CONTRADICTION FLAGGED, not resolved: Doerr says Froebe-Kapteyn knew Derleth 'mindestens seit 1910', while Jost (1965, p. 74) dates the acquaintance to 1916. The letter is sent from The Hague; the stop is pinned to Munich, where Derleth received it. CORRECTION: the phrase Doerr quotes is 'maitre fabuleux', without a circumflex.
stops.campa: A letter reaches him headed Haag, 27. Aug. 20. It is the first of the surviving correspondence from Olga Froebe-Kapteyn and the sequence runs twenty-eight years, ending only at his death. She calls him her fabulous master. She writes as a disciple to a mystagogue and, again and again, as a woman in love with a man who is not going to answer in kind. Almost nothing of his side survives. The archive at Marbach holds her voice and his silence, in that proportion.
stops.quote_source: Olga Froebe-Kapteyn to Ludwig Derleth, Derleth-Nachlass, Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach, quoted in Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona'
suggested_refs: The Froebe-Kapteyn letters in the Derleth-Nachlass, Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach
sources: Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona' (georgdoerr.net)
Dominik Jost, Ludwig Derleth: Gestalt und Leistung (1965), p. 74

stops.name: Ascona, the wolf at Monte Tabor
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the visit to Villa Monte Tabor, reported through Christine Derleth's memoir as summarized in secondary literature; the villa's precise location was not confirmed and the coordinate is the Ascona centroid per OSM/Nominatim (46.1554, 8.7708). The May 1921 letter is attested in Doerr from the Marbach Nachlass. A second sheet, without salutation, dated 3 Aug. 21, reads 'Könnte ich eine Fackel in dein Blut werfen, daß es über mich ausbräche wie der Strom des feurigen Berges!'; a widely circulated transcription giving 'ausbreche' for the subjunctive 'ausbräche' is wrong and is corrected here.
stops.campa: He visits her above Ascona at the house she has named Monte Tabor, after the mountain of the Transfiguration. Her letters of these months ask him to stroke his obedient she-wolf, and wish she could throw a torch into his blood so that it would break over her like the stream off a burning mountain. He is fifty, married to nobody, formed by an asceticism that has already refused him once at an official door. What he answers is not in the archive. He kept no copies; she kept everything.
stops.quote: Jetzt komme ich wieder in den Bereich der Herrlichkeit. Bitte streichle Deine gehorsame Wolfin.
stops.quote_source: Olga Froebe-Kapteyn to Ludwig Derleth, May 1921, Derleth-Nachlass, Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach, quoted in Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona'
suggested_refs: Villa Monte Tabor, Ascona, location not independently confirmed
sources: Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona' (georgdoerr.net)
Christine Derleth, Das Fleischlich-Geistige (1973), as reported in secondary literature

stops.name: Rome, October 1922
stops.date_confidence: Attested, but the usual citation is wrong. The source is Dominik Jost, Ludwig Derleth: Gestalt und Leistung (Stuttgart, 1965), p. 103, quoted verbatim in Georg Doerr: 'Im Oktober 1922, waehrend des Aufenthaltes in Ascona, reiste Ludwig Derleth mit Olga Froebe nach Rom.' Deutsche Biographie, often cited for it, contains no such chronology. The juxtaposition with the March on Rome of 28-30 October 1922 is this file's, not a source's: no reaction by Derleth to the March, then or later, is recorded anywhere reached. Coordinate is about 250 m from the Rome centroid.
stops.campa: In October, during a stay at Ascona, he travels to Rome with Olga Froebe-Kapteyn. At the end of that same month Mussolini's columns converge on the city and the king hands him the government. Nothing in the record connects the two facts. Derleth leaves no comment on the March on Rome, then or later. For eighteen years he has been proclaiming an imperial order under the Church, and men with far better logistics are now installing something shaped like one. Whether he took that for vindication or for theft, the papers do not say.
suggested_refs: Dominik Jost, Ludwig Derleth: Gestalt und Leistung (Stuttgart, 1965), p. 103
sources: Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona' (georgdoerr.net), note 3, quoting Jost 1965 p. 103

stops.name: Rome, the marriage to Christine Ulrich
stops.date_confidence: [R] for the exact date of 15 March 1924, which comes from the Wikipedia articles and was not confirmed against a register. The church or civil office is identified in nothing reachable, and general Rome coordinates are used. Christine Ulrich's birth at Darmstadt in 1894 and her parentage are likewise [R] from the same articles.
stops.campa: He marries Christine Ulrich in Rome. He is fifty-three, she is twenty-nine, daughter of Christian Ulrich and Maria Baartz of Darmstadt and sister of his friend Wilhelm. She will keep his papers, sit out thirteen Ticino winters with him, outlive him by decades, and write the memoir that remains the only intimate account of the man and the least trustworthy document about him. Which church or registry performed the marriage is named in nothing that can be read today.
stops.quote: Sie [i.e. Katja Pringsheim] war die Tochter des Munchener Mathematik-Professors Pringsheim, in dessen Haus Ludwig Derleth ebenso verkehrte, wie er Frau Senator Mann (Mutter von Thomas Mann) kannte. Katja hegte zarte Gefuhle fur Ludwig Derleth, der aber keine Ehe eingehen wollte.
stops.quote_source: Christine Derleth, Das Fleischlich-Geistige: Meine Erinnerungen an Ludwig Derleth (Bellnhausen ueber Gladenbach, 1973), p. 183, quoted in Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona'. The memoir goes on to derive Thomas Mann's hostility to Derleth from this episode; that causal claim is the doubtful part, since Mann's first satire of him, Gladius Dei, is 1902 and Katia married Mann in 1905.
suggested_refs: Christine Derleth, Das Fleischlich-Geistige (1973)
sources: Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona' (georgdoerr.net), note 21

stops.name: Munich, leaving for good
stops.date_confidence: CONTRADICTION FLAGGED, not resolved. English Wikipedia dates the permanent departure from Munich to about 1924; Literaturportal Bayern says 'Ab 1925' for Rome, Basel and Perchtoldsdorf, and das-blaettchen also gives Rome from 1925. 1925 is used here as the better-attested of the two.
stops.campa: He leaves Munich for good. He has lived there on and off for something over thirty years: the university, the school service, Schwabing, the cosmics, the readings, the sister, the whole apparatus of a reputation built and then endured. From here he is a writer with no country of residence, moving between Rome, Basel, and a market town outside Vienna, carrying a manuscript that keeps growing for the next twenty years and is never finished in any sense he would accept as finished.
suggested_refs: Literaturportal Bayern's 'Ab 1925' chronology for Rome, Basel and Perchtoldsdorf

stops.name: Basel, the city on the Rhine bend
stops.date_confidence: Residence attested (das-blaettchen; Literaturportal Bayern), undated; 1926 is an ordering device. Coordinate matches the Basel pin used in nietzsche.journey.json (47.559, 7.589). The debt to Nietzsche is a textual, one-directional influence relation attested in the standard accounts of the Proklamationen's form, not a meeting: Nietzsche died in 1900, before Derleth's own Basel period, and Derleth is not on record naming him.
stops.campa: For a period nobody has dated he lives at Basel. It is the city where Nietzsche held a chair at twenty-four and wrote The Birth of Tragedy, and Nietzsche is the writer whose form Derleth took over entire for the Proklamationen: the prophetic voice, the commanding aphorism, the speaker who legislates instead of arguing. Nietzsche died in 1900 and never breathed Basel air while Derleth was in it. The debt runs one way only, and Derleth never once acknowledges it by name.
suggested_refs: Friedrich Nietzsche's Basel chair and Die Geburt der Tragoedie, the formal model behind the Proklamationen

stops.name: Perchtoldsdorf, the Frankish Koran under the Vienna Woods
stops.date_confidence: CONTRADICTION FLAGGED, not resolved: de.wikipedia's Perchtoldsdorf article says he lived there 'zwischen 1928 und 1935', while das-blaettchen gives 1927 to 1935. Coordinate corrected from 48.1167, 16.2667, which sat about 2.3 km northeast of the market town and over the Vienna city line; Perchtoldsdorf geocodes to 48.1038, 16.2418 (OSM/Nominatim).
stops.campa: In a wine-growing market town at the edge of the Vienna Woods he settles for seven or eight years and writes the enormous book. Der fraenkische Koran is a recitation: Franconia, his own province of vineyards and prince-bishops, given the form of a world scripture, five hundred pages of prose and verse built to be read aloud as revelation. The title is a claim about genre and not a conversion. He is no Muslim, has never been one, and there is no evidence he ever saw Mecca.
suggested_refs: de.wikipedia, 'Perchtoldsdorf', on Derleth's residence there

stops.name: Weimar, the Frankish Koran printed
stops.date_confidence: DATE CONFLICT FLAGGED: de.wikipedia and Literaturportal Bayern give 1932, Deutsche Biographie and the NDB give 1933; not resolved. K10plus records Weimar, Lichtenstein, 1932, VII, 506 S. CORRECTION: the frequent claim that the Weimar printing was partial and later completed at Kassel is unsupported, the Weimar 1932 and Kassel 1933 records carrying identical collations; and 'Des Werkes erster Teil' is the subtitle of the 1971 Hinder & Deelmann volume, not of the 1932 book. Publication-site stop; personal travel to Weimar is not established. Coordinate is about 440 m from the Weimar centroid.
stops.campa: Der fraenkische Koran is printed at Weimar by Lichtenstein: seven pages of front matter and five hundred and six of text. It is the largest thing he ever completes, and it goes on sale in a Germany with ten months of its republic left to run. Reichstag elections in July, more in November, street fighting through both. A book proposing a Catholic imperial order recited as scripture arrives in the middle of that and is noticed by almost nobody. The Kassel imprint follows within the year.
suggested_refs: Der fraenkische Koran (Weimar: Lichtenstein, 1932), VII + 506 pp.
sources: K10plus catalogue records for Der fraenkische Koran

stops.name: Kassel, the Baerenreiter edition
stops.date_confidence: Attested: K10plus holds two Kassel, Baerenreiter, 1933 records for Der fraenkische Koran, VII, 506 S., the same collation as the Weimar 1932 record. The 1932 versus 1933 conflict noted at the Weimar stop applies here as well. Publication-site stop; personal travel to Kassel is not established. That readers found fascism in the book is an interpretive statement about its reception, not a claim about Derleth's politics, on which see the Sibylline Book stop.
stops.campa: Baerenreiter at Kassel issues the same five hundred and six pages under its own imprint. The year is 1933. His book of an armed and hierarchical Christendom is now on German shelves under a government that has just claimed every hierarchy in the country for itself, and any reader wanting to find fascism in the Fraenkischer Koran will not have to search. His own verdict on the new order gets written two years later, in a manuscript no publisher ever sees.
suggested_refs: Der fraenkische Koran (Kassel: Baerenreiter-Verlag, 1933), VII + 506 pp.
sources: K10plus catalogue records for Der fraenkische Koran

stops.name: San Pietro di Stabio, the palazzo on the frontier
stops.date_confidence: Attested for the year and the residence (de.wikipedia; en.wikipedia; Cantone Ticino, 'Oltreconfiniti'). No documentary evidence establishes flight from a specific personal threat, only the coincidence with the Nazi seizure of power in Germany. COORDINATE CORRECTED and standardized for this file: 45.8494, 8.9349 is the village of Stabio, not the San Pietro quarter where he lived and died; the Chiesa di San Pietro, Via Dogana 16, geocodes to 45.8592, 8.9357 (OSM/Nominatim), and 45.859, 8.936 is used for every San Pietro stop here. A circulating afterlife pin of 45.8656, 8.9425 for the same place, about 1.9 km away, is discarded.
stops.campa: He crosses into neutral Switzerland and takes a large palazzo at San Pietro di Stabio, a hamlet on the Mendrisiotto plain a kilometre from the Italian border and its customs post. He is sixty-four. He will not leave again. Thirteen years in one house, after fifty-five years of being moved on. The Ticino canton keeps a register of foreigners who ended up inside its borders, and it files him there under a phrase that does for the whole life: a long wandering, concluded at San Pietro di Stabio.
stops.quote: Un lungo peregrinare conclusosi a San Pietro di Stabio.
stops.quote_source: Cantone Ticino, 'Oltreconfiniti: le celebrita internazionali in Ticino', Personaggi uid 47
suggested_refs: Cantone Ticino, 'Oltreconfiniti', www4.ti.ch/can/oltreconfiniti

stops.name: San Pietro di Stabio, Die Lebensalter
stops.date_confidence: Attested. K10plus: 'Die Lebensalter [Gedichte]', Kassel, Baerenreiter-Verlag, 1937, 112 S. CORRECTION: the book was published in Germany, not in Switzerland as several accounts state; the writing, not the printing, is what belongs at San Pietro. The stop is pinned at Derleth's own residence for that reason.
stops.campa: Baerenreiter at Kassel prints Die Lebensalter, a hundred and twelve pages of poems written here in seclusion. The ages of life: childhood, youth, manhood, age, the oldest scheme in European verse, handled by a man of sixty-seven who has spent forty years addressing an order that never enrolled a single member. The manuscript goes north from a Swiss village to a German publisher in the fourth year of the Reich, and nothing in it names the Reich. A hundred and twelve pages, Baerenreiter, Kassel, 1937.
suggested_refs: Die Lebensalter (Kassel: Baerenreiter-Verlag, 1937), 112 pp.

stops.name: San Pietro di Stabio, the Sibylline Book
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The Hitler passage in the 'Sibyllinisches Buch' is reported in secondary Derleth scholarship as summarized in reference works and was not independently located or read; it appears in none of the sources reached, neither Deutsche Biographie nor Literaturportal Bayern. The composition period is variously given as about 1935 to 1940; 1938 is an ordering date. The work was not published in his lifetime.
stops.campa: In a manuscript he does not publish, the Sibyllinisches Buch, he writes Hitler down: a blind destroyer of the order of history and of peace, a man who fills an abyss with corpses. It is his verdict on the movement his own vocabulary of empire, hierarchy and consecrated violence had spent thirty years supplying in advance. He puts the pages in a drawer in a village on the Italian frontier, and they stay in that drawer through the war and past his death.
suggested_refs: The unpublished 'Sibyllinisches Buch', Derleth-Nachlass, Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach
sources: Reported tradition in secondary Derleth scholarship as summarized in reference works, not independently located

stops.name: San Pietro di Stabio, Seraphinische Hochzeit
stops.date_confidence: Attested. K10plus: 'Seraphinische Hochzeit', Ludwig Derleth, Salzburg and Leipzig, Mueller, 1939, 172 S., with a review the same year in Stimmen der Zeit 136 (1939), no. 9, p. 200. CORRECTION: the book was published at Salzburg and Leipzig, not in Switzerland as several accounts state; the writing is what belongs at San Pietro.
stops.campa: Seraphinische Hochzeit appears from Mueller at Salzburg and Leipzig, a hundred and seventy-two pages of visions and parables in mixed prose and verse, and a Jesuit review notices it in Stimmen der Zeit the same year. Austria has been part of Germany for a year when the book is set, and Poland is invaded in September. The seraphic wedding is the mystical marriage of the soul, and this is the last of his books to be printed on the German-speaking side of the border.
suggested_refs: Seraphinische Hochzeit (Salzburg and Leipzig: Mueller, 1939), 172 pp.
Review in Stimmen der Zeit 136 (1939), no. 9, p. 200

stops.name: Lucerne, the death of Thanatos
stops.date_confidence: BIBLIOGRAPHIC CONFLICT FLAGGED, not resolved: both Wikipedias list 1945 for Der Tod des Thanatos from Josef Stocker in Lucerne, while other bibliographies give 1946. Publication-site stop, pinned to Lucerne; Derleth's own travel there is not established.
stops.campa: Josef Stocker at Lucerne publishes Der Tod des Thanatos, a meditation on sin, killing, war, and the conquest of death, in the year the war ends. The death of death is a technical Christian phrase, the defeat of the last enemy at the resurrection, and he means it technically. The publisher is a Catholic house in a Catholic canton. He is seventy-five. He has spent the whole conflict a kilometre from a fascist state, on the neutral side of a customs post, writing about killing.
suggested_refs: Der Tod des Thanatos (Lucerne: Josef Stocker, 1945 or 1946)

stops.name: San Pietro di Stabio, the last portrait
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The pencil portrait by the Dutch artist Haro op van Veld is reported in the consulted secondary record and cross-referenced against Stadtarchiv Gerolzhofen holdings; it was not independently examined, and the October 1947 date is confirmed by no source reached.
stops.campa: The Dutch artist Haro op van Veld draws him in pencil in the last autumn: an old man in a large cold house on a plain, four months from dying. The sheet travels afterwards to the local collection in Gerolzhofen, four hundred kilometres north, in the town where he was born and where a street will one day carry his name. It is the last likeness taken from the living face, forty-three years after Kolbe cut his head in stone in Munich. Pencil on paper, one sheet.
suggested_refs: Haro op van Veld's pencil portrait of Derleth, Stadtarchiv Gerolzhofen holdings
sources: Deutsche Biographie chronology cross-referenced with Stadtarchiv Gerolzhofen holdings, not independently examined

stops.name: San Pietro di Stabio, the circles close
stops.date_confidence: Attested that the last letter exists and is on ERANOS TAGUNGEN letterhead; Doerr dates it 'Letzter Brief, wohl kurz vor dem Tod Derleths im Jahre 1948', so December 1947 is an ordering date and not a documented one. [R] for the claim that Derleth never attended the Eranos meetings at Casa Gabriella, which comes from Christine Derleth's memoir and is unconfirmed. Eranos was founded in 1933 with C. G. Jung and Rudolf Otto in the credited founding roles; Derleth's part, per Derleth-focused literature, was an earlier formation of Froebe-Kapteyn's reading, Bachofen and Creuzer and the ancient mysteries, and not a founding one. CORRECTION: the quotation marks around 'Rosengarten des Blutes' are in the original and mark a phrase she is citing back to him; transcriptions that drop them make it her coinage.
stops.campa: The last letter from Olga Froebe-Kapteyn comes on the printed letterhead of the Eranos conferences, the institution she built at Ascona out of the mythography he first put into her hands, and which by his own widow's later account he never once attended. She writes that the circles are closing, that meeting him belongs among the timelessly beautiful things of her life, that she has forgotten nothing. Then she quotes a phrase of his own back at him: a rose garden of blood.
stops.quote: Ludwig - Die Kreise schließen sich. Zu den zeitlos schönen Dingen meines Lebens gehört die Begegnung mit Ihnen. Ich habe nichts vergessen - In dem reichen Leben von heute liegt jenes Erlebnis wie eine verborgene Kostbarkeit, - ein 'Rosengarten des Blutes'. Olga.
stops.quote_source: Olga Froebe-Kapteyn, last letter to Ludwig Derleth, on ERANOS TAGUNGEN letterhead, shortly before his death in 1948, Derleth-Nachlass, Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach, quoted in Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona'
suggested_refs: The Eranos conferences at Ascona, founded 1933
Christine Derleth, Das Fleischlich-Geistige (1973), on Derleth's non-attendance
sources: Georg Doerr, 'Archetyp und Geschichte oder Muenchen-Ascona' (georgdoerr.net)

stops.name: San Pietro di Stabio, death and the missing grave
stops.date_confidence: Attested for date, place and age: 13 January 1948 at San Pietro di Stabio, aged 77 (Deutsche Biographie; de.wikipedia; en.wikipedia). No reliable cause of death is established in any accessible source. The burial is an open gap in the record, stated here as a gap rather than as a claim that the grave is lost: no cemetery, headstone or grave fate appears in Deutsche Biographie, either Wikipedia, the Kalliope authority record for GND 11852478X, or the Ticino Oltreconfiniti page.
stops.campa: He dies at San Pietro di Stabio on the thirteenth of January, seventy-seven years old. No cause of death is established in any accessible source. No cemetery is named, no headstone described, no account given of whether a grave survives or was cleared: not by Deutsche Biographie, not by either Wikipedia, not by the Kalliope authority record, not by the Ticino canton's own page about him. Where the body of the man who spent fifty years proclaiming an order now lies is simply not on record.
suggested_refs: Parish and communal burial registers of Stabio, not consulted

stops.name: Gerolzhofen, the street and the six volumes
stops.date_confidence: Das Werk attested: K10plus title statement, verbatim, 'Das Werk sechs Baende / Ludwig Derleth. [In Verbindung mit Christine Derleth hrsg. von Dominik Jost]', Bellnhausen ueber Gladenbach (Hessen), Hinder & Deelmann, 1971-1972. CONTRADICTION FLAGGED: en.wikipedia calls the same edition seven volumes; six is the catalogued figure and the outlier is the English article. [R] for the street and the school: the Ludwig-Derleth-Realschule is in en.wikipedia, the birth-house street detail rests on local sources not independently confirmed, and neither naming is dated by any source reached. 1971 is an ordering date. Balthasar's essay 'Integralismus' is 1963 and is cited here as later engagement with the work, not as an event in Derleth's life.
stops.campa: The town of his birth puts his name on the street of his birth house and on a Realschule. In the same years his widow and Dominik Jost bring out Das Werk from Hinder und Deelmann at Bellnhausen, six volumes across 1971 and 1972, though the English catalogues insist on seven and nobody has reconciled them. Franconia takes him back as a local author. In Basel, meanwhile, a theologian has been reading the Proklamationen as a specimen of Catholic integralism and quoting them at length in order to answer them.
stops.quote: It is better not to be born than to be idle. But once you are the light, illuminate the darkness.
stops.quote_source: Ludwig Derleth, Proklamationen (1904), quoted in Hans Urs von Balthasar, 'Integralismus' (1963), trans. Charles Hughes Huff and Anne Carpenter, theologyandsociety.com. Opening line of the block Balthasar introduces with 'It is worth listening to this voice a little (I quote at random)'.
suggested_refs: Das Werk, 6 vols., ed. Dominik Jost with Christine Derleth (Bellnhausen: Hinder & Deelmann, 1971-1972)
Hans Urs von Balthasar, 'Integralismus' (1963)
The Ludwig-Derleth-Realschule, Gerolzhofen
